{\bf The main Thoerem B} (an extension)\quad Let $p\geq 5$. Then $p$ is odd.

{\bf The main Theorem B'}\quad Let $p\geq 7$. Then $p$ is odd.

\textbf{Linearity Criterion:}
\emph{A map is affine when its second derivative is zero.}

The bound follows from
$$ a = b + c $$
{\bf Case I}. Suppose that $d$ is odd. Then the bound holds
by the sum above.
{\bf Case II}. Suppose that $d$ is even. Then the sum is one.

{\bf{Case (a): \; $H=P\times B$ for an abelian group $B$.}}\\
Then $H$ is nilpotent.

{\bf{Case (b): \; $H=Q\times B$ for a prime $q$.}}\\
Then $H$ is nilpotent too.
